title: The Frobenius of the structure sheaf is a morphism of locally ringed spaces; affine case
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number. (i) Let $A$ be a commutative ring with $p\cdot1=0$ and $F_A:A\to A$, $a\mapsto a^p$, its Frobenius endomorphism. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subseteq A$, $F_A^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p$; hence the continuous map of $\operatorname{Spec}(F_A):\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the identity. (ii) If moreover $A$ is local, $F_A$ is a local homomorphism. (iii) Let $X$ be a scheme with $p=0$ in $\mathcal O_X$. The maps $F_{\mathcal O_X(U)}$, $U\subseteq X$ open, form an endomorphism $F^\sharp$ of the sheaf of rings $\mathcal O_X$ whose map on the stalk at $x$ is $F_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}$; consequently $(\mathrm{id}_X,F^\sharp):X\to X$ is a morphism of locally ringed spaces, hence an endomorphism of the scheme $X$. (iv) If $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $p=0$ in $A$, this endomorphism equals $\operatorname{Spec}(F_A)$; more generally, for an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ the endomorphism $(\mathrm{id}_X,F^\sharp)$ restricts to the corresponding endomorphism of $U$, and for an affine open $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ that restriction is $\operatorname{Spec}(F_A)$. The same holds for the iterates, with $a\mapsto a^{p^n}$.

source.place: Varieties, Section 33.36 (tag 0CC6), the paragraph after Definition 33.36.1 (tag 03SM): 'This makes sense because for any ring $A$ of characteristic $p$ the map $F_A$ ... induces the identity on $\Spec(A)$. Moreover, if $A$ is local, then $F_A$ is a local homomorphism'; parts (iii)-(iv) are not stated in Stacks

proof.text: For (i), use the ring endomorphism $F_A(a)=a^p$ of [def-weil-ring-frobenius]. If $a\in\mathfrak p$ then $a^p\in\mathfrak p$ by closure of an ideal under multiplication. Conversely, for every integer $r\geq1$, primality gives $a^r\in\mathfrak p\Rightarrow a\in\mathfrak p$: induct on $r$, using $a^{r+1}=a\,a^r$ and the defining implication $bc\in\mathfrak p\Rightarrow b\in\mathfrak p$ or $c\in\mathfrak p$. Since $p\geq1$, this proves $a\in F_A^{-1}(\mathfrak p)\Leftrightarrow a\in\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius), following paragraph, first two sentences; elementary prime-ideal argument written out.

proof.text: By the definition of the map on spectra induced by a ring homomorphism, its value at $\mathfrak p$ is the inverse-image prime ideal. Thus Step 1 shows that the underlying continuous map of $\operatorname{Spec}(F_A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] fixes every point, and is the identity. If $A$ is the zero ring, its spectrum is empty and the same conclusion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius), following paragraph: the ring Frobenius induces the identity on Spec(A).

proof.text: For (ii), write $\mathfrak m$ for the unique maximal ideal of the local ring $A$. If $a\in\mathfrak m$, then $F_A(a)=a^p\in\mathfrak m$ by the ideal property, so $F_A$ maps the maximal ideal into itself and is local in the sense of [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. One can also check the unit-reflection formulation directly: if $a^pb=1$, then $a(a^{p-1}b)=1$, so $a$ is a unit; if $a$ is a unit, $(a^{-1})^p$ inverts $a^p$. No reducedness or perfection is used.

source.place: Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius), following paragraph: if A is local then F_A is a local homomorphism; elementary ideal and unit calculations.

proof.text: For (iii), [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p] gives $p\cdot1=0$ in every $\mathcal O_X(U)$. Apply [def-weil-ring-frobenius] to define $\psi_U(s)=s^p$ as a ring endomorphism, including when $U=\varnothing$. For an inclusion $V\subseteq U$, the restriction ring homomorphism $\rho_{UV}$ satisfies $\rho_{UV}(s^p)=\rho_{UV}(s)^p$ (multiply $s$ by itself $p$ times). Therefore $\rho_{UV}\psi_U=\psi_V\rho_{UV}$. These are exactly the restriction-compatibility equations for a map of sheaves of rings in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], so the maps define $F^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius) and following paragraph; restriction compatibility is the ring-map power identity also used in the proof of Tag 0CC7 (lemma-frobenius-endomorphism-identity).

proof.text: Compute on germs to identify the stalk map. An element of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is represented by a pair $(U,s)$ with $x\in U$, two pairs being equal if their sections agree after restriction to some common neighbourhood of $x$. Step 4 shows that $[U,s]\mapsto[U,s^p]$ respects this relation. Ring operations on germs are computed on a common neighbourhood, so $[U,s^p]=[U,s]^p$; also $p\cdot1=0$ on germs because it is zero on sections. Hence the stalk map is precisely the Frobenius of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. This stalk is local since $X$ is a locally ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Step 3 applies to this stalk ring, so its Frobenius is local.

source.place: Tags 0078 (section-stalks) and 007G (section-stalks-presheaves-structures), explicit description by germs and ring operations; applied to the map in Tag 03SM.

proof.text: The identity of the underlying topological space is continuous. Combine it with the sheaf map of Step 4 and the local stalk maps of Step 5. The identity-on-space criterion in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] now says exactly that $(\mathrm{id}_X,F^\sharp)$ is a morphism of locally ringed spaces. A morphism between schemes is such a morphism of their underlying locally ringed spaces, so this is a scheme endomorphism, as required in (iii).

source.place: Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius), following paragraph: this defines an endomorphism in the category of schemes; Schemes Tag 01HB (definition-locally-ringed-space).

proof.text: For the affine assertion in (iv), let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Under $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=A$, the map on global sections of the scheme endomorphism constructed in Step 6 is $a\mapsto a^p$. The affine-spectrum correspondence of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] says that morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ are uniquely determined by their induced ring homomorphisms on global sections. The endomorphism constructed in Step 6 and $\operatorname{Spec}(F_A)$ both induce $F_A$, so they are equal.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine), bijection taking a morphism to its map on global sections; used to identify the construction of Tag 03SM on an affine scheme.

proof.text: For an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$, its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_X|_U$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus for every open $V\subseteq U$ the restricted sheaf endomorphism sends the same section $s\in\mathcal O_U(V)=\mathcal O_X(V)$ to $s^p$. The restricted underlying map is the identity of $U$. Hence this restriction is exactly the endomorphism constructed for $U$ in Steps 4–6. If $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, identify its global sections with $A$ by that isomorphism: any ring isomorphism preserves powers, so Step 7 identifies this restriction with $\operatorname{Spec}(F_A)$.

source.place: Tag 01HE (definition-immersion-locally-ringed-spaces), open subspaces with restricted structure sheaf, and Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine); applied to the sectionwise formula of Varieties Tag 03SM.

proof.text: Finally, for every integer $n\geq0$, form the $n$-fold composite, starting at $n=0$ with the identity. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subseteq A$, induction using Step 1 gives $(F_A^n)^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p$: the base is the identity map and the successor inverse image is $F_A^{-1}((F_A^n)^{-1}(\mathfrak p))=F_A^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p$. For local $A$, each $F_A^n$ maps the maximal ideal into itself by repeated application of Step 3. By the composition formula in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], it has identity underlying map and section map $F_{\mathcal O_X(V)}^n$. The iterate formula in [def-weil-ring-frobenius] gives $s\mapsto s^{p^n}$: the induction step is $(s^{p^n})^p=s^{p^{n+1}}$. For a germ represented by $(U,s)$, the $n$-fold stalk composite sends $[U,s]$ to $[U,s^{p^n}]$, which equals $[U,s]^{p^n}$ by the germ ring operations. Each composite remains local because a composite of maps carrying maximal ideals into maximal ideals does so. On an open $U$, the restricted section map is still $s\mapsto s^{p^n}$ on every open subset of $U$. On an affine open, functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies the composite with $\operatorname{Spec}(F_A^n)$. This proves all the iterate assertions, including $n=0$ and the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 03SM (definition-absolute-frobenius), sectionwise formula, iterated by composition; elementary exponent and restriction computations.
